title: Legacy of the Era
subtitle:
A worm frozen in resin, its body encased for hundreds of millions of years.
Is it the prisoner within this silent amber or a creation of eternity?

trails.title: Where Does the Skylark Rest
trails.description: Winter is coming, yet under the Golden Famine, the long river runs pale and weak.

content.text: Look at these boys. They left home with puffed chests and confident smiles on their faces—
Thinking they'd go to the front, pull a few triggers, kill a few enemies, and come back as heroes.
But when their feet hit the soil, they turned "pacifist," it seems, wounding their own hands rather than their enemies'.
Their mothers should have begged them to stay, not waved their handkerchiefs to see them off.

branch.text: Soldiers follow orders, officers give them, higher-ups make them, parents send their children off to die ...
And not one of them will bear the weight of their "misjudgments." Only the dead must answer.
Really? You think death is the only option?
What could possibly be the point in that?
Don't tell me you believe there's GLORY in dying on the battlefield? The thought makes me sick.
Look there—at the lifeless body lying flat in the mud.
He couldn't even muster the courage to flee, so he bribed a fellow soldier—a man he barely knew—with three cigarettes to surrender with him.
He died—killed in a moment of pure, senseless hatred. And the other lived—saved by a flicker of mercy.
Where should his mother aim her grief? At the officer who changed his mind just a moment too late? Hah!
The officer will be pardoned; they'll say he, too, was a victim of this endless, miserable cycle of hatred.
So tell me—please, tell me—to whom this rage should go, and I will take this kitchen knife and plunge it into their heart!

items.text: Legacy of the Era
Street, Bereggrad
Bereggrad receives the thundering hooves of the cavalry in dead silence. It's as if the city has been deserted.

Yet the soldiers sense the stares—frightened, alert, resentful—peering through every rusted doorway, every shattered stained-glass window. They settle on the weary warhorses, on dust-stained uniforms, and on the black barrels of their guns.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: What are they so scared of? The cavalry's here to protect them.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: After all the chaos—letters from the front, soaring prices, bandits, Bereggrad is worn thin, even afraid of its own shadow.

items.speaker: Sternova
items.text: *sigh* Just like the people of Tamarovka.
The commander looks up at the shuttered windows around him, then turns to the shadows hiding in the alleys.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: You didn't keep the cavalry's orders confidential?
Igor walks beside him. From time to time, he presses against his ribs, where the sting of the gunshot still echoes.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Word always gets out.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Then the citizens must know that you will soon withdraw from the Don. With no one left to protect them, they have lost all faith.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: They do not know why the cavalry comes. I'm certain their minds are filled with the worst possibilities.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: They think you will plunder the city, no doubt. That's most of what they have faced since this began.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: I see. I'll find a man of standing. Fyodor Petrovich, perhaps. And convince him we bear no ill.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: People don't understand what they cannot see with their own eyes, and you cannot tell them about the Foundation or Zeno.
In the darkness, several citizens lurk with weapons in their hands. Not one of them escapes Igor's eyes.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: They have already formed a militia, preparing for the worst. All we can do is remain discreet and avoid adding fuel to the fire.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: We must end this quickly. Deal with Krutov. Captured or killed, it doesn't matter. Destroy their ritual, and return the steppe to what she once was.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: And aid the Timekeeper in her mission.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: One week, Igor. That was your word. Do not forget it.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I suggest we entrust the ritual issue to Lilya's flight unit.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: They have the element of surprise. An aerial strike will give the Manus little time to react.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: Already done. The coordinates you gave are with Lieutenant Lilya. She's working on an air raid plan as we speak.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I will leave Bereggrad to you. The Timekeeper waits for me at the church.

items.speaker: Commander Ivan
items.text: What she seeks is in a church?
Lilya brings her broom to a stop outside a church.

This church is unremarkable among the many others in Bereggrad—medium-sized and without a distinctive dome. Only its position sets it apart. It stands on higher ground, giving it a clear overlook of the golden plains.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What kind of church is this? Place is abandoned.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Captain, I don't know what you're looking for here, but you got to take care of yourself, especially ...
As she glances over, she spots Igor approaching from afar.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I will, Lilya. Have a good flight.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Never had a bad one.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Though smashing into the vice president's office would make it a little better than the rest.
It's a farewell in Lilya's own style. But she doesn't leave. Instead, she fixes her gaze on Igor.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Lieutenant Lilya, my interests do not conflict with the Timekeeper's. The coordinates I provided are correct. We're on the same side.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I am not worried. If you dare to lie about this, you're not leaving the city alive.
Lilya steps forward, directly squaring up with the rebel leader.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But no matter what you do, now or in the future, I'll never forget what you did in São Paulo.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I'll live through this war, and I hope you do too, so I can walk you to the judgment seat myself and see you punished for everything you've done.
She meets his eyes head-on, like an eagle locking onto its prey.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And if the court doesn't sentence you to death, I will.
Meeting Lilya's eyes, Igor understands that this isn't a threat but a declaration.
He doesn't confront her, but he doesn't avoid her gaze either.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Lieutenant, I know what I've done. I see the faces of those I sacrificed more clearly than anyone.
A suffocating stillness settles across his face.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I look forward to my judgment day.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: So do I.
Lilya mounts her broom and takes off. Igor watches as she rises into the sky and rejoins her squad.
He lowers his head.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Let's go, Timekeeper. What you search for is underneath the church.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Underneath?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: As eras change, so do landmarks. There was a time the Amber Room was buried beneath a market, even.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The church's cellar is deep, near the periphery of the Amber Room. Ptolemy led the digging of a simple tunnel between them.
Just as they are about to set off, Sonetto lets out her anxious hesitation.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, are you sure you want to go down there alone?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's alright, Sonetto. Only Igor and I are allowed in the Amber Room. That was the deal.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You and Marsha can just wait for me here.
The road down is not long, but the darkness of the suffocating earth devours any sense of time.
Guided by the lingering scent of gunpowder from Ptolemy's excavation, they move toward a faint point of light in the distance.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What's that light ahead?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The lighting system my men built before.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Before? When they dug the tunnel?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Earlier than that.
The light grows brighter, revealing an unexpectedly complex structure as they pass through the entryway.
Metro Station, Bereggrad
It appears to be a vast subway station or some grand theatrical stage.
Whether or not an ode has ever been sung here, this is clearly not something that could have been built in this era.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A metro station. Looks like Cold War period. What's it doing here?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: It's because of the Amber Room. The range of its "Storm" immunity expanded, covering this station.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The immunity range expanded. So this isn't the center of the Amber Room?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Of course not. There was a metro station here when the Foundation and Zeno built the laboratory.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A laboratory built in collaboration between the Foundation and Zeno?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: There is still some distance to the Amber Room. Let's talk on the way. Much remains to explain.
Now they've entered the subway station. The aged Zeno traitor finally seems to shed the veiled wording in his speech.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The Foundation and Zeno have worked on many projects together of many security levels. I am now free to talk of them.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: After the second "Storm," several Zeno generals and Committee members requested my military support for a research project on the "Storm."

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: At first, I thought it was similar to the Changeling project. Shady, perhaps, but not too harmful.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That project still caused harm to tourists at the Green Lake Campsite and the surrounding residents.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: This is nothing compared to what the Amber Room did.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: After I joined the project, my orders were to station on the outskirts of Bereggrad and build a military zone to protect the underground site.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: At the same time, the Foundation asked for a thorough review of all soldiers who served Zeno after the first "Storm" but did not appear in any 1999 records at headquarters.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Were they not registered?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: No. Their records were flawless in each branch across the world. But compared to headquarters' records from 1999, anomalies were found.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Some had similar resumes and ranks but different photos from those filed in headquarters, as if their identities were stolen or replaced.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Zeno also encountered people whose faces matched the archive but whose names were different, with no connection to Zeno at all.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Sound familiar, Timekeeper?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes, Mr. Duncan in São Paulo. His appearance matched an acquaintance of mine, a man I saw dissolve in the "Storm."

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I was tasked with locating these abnormalities and bringing them to the Amber Room. For what purpose, I did not know.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The guard there confided to me that people looked different after leaving, as if no longer themselves.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Did you ever consider finding out what was going on?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: No. Back then, my faith was firm. I wholeheartedly believed in the Foundation's vision of peace and honored my duty. That is to say, I followed orders.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: That led to my deepest regret. After the sixth "Storm," they brought in Urd.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The Foundation found Urd that long ago?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Specifically, those leading the Amber Room Project did. By order of the Pax House, all information on the project was sealed.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The two subsequent "Storms" came suddenly. During that time, something happened to Urd, something different.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: During one "Storm," she escaped, but the secrecy of the project left us without manpower to find her.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: This is what led to her multiple disappearances in the following "Storms."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She could've stayed in the safe zone, couldn't she?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Indeed. From my view, the Foundation only searched for her to cover for their mistakes.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I remember well the last time I saw Urd. It was on a vast land, dangerous, barren, much like the Don steppe.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: In Antarctica?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: That was Doctor Dores. I talk of Urd.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: When I saw her in São Paulo, I knew her at once. Both by her appearance and by her unique calm bravery.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: But Doctor Dores was not the woman I knew in 1999. She was lost. A soul trying to reclaim memory and identity.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: In other words, the last time you saw the Urd you knew was before the first "Storm."

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Correct. In 1999, the year the first "Storm" rose rain from the earth. This is the second event I want to tell you about.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: At that time, our army stood ready in Kazakhstan for a war none had ever seen before.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Ms. Urd, the army is combat ready.

items.speaker: Urd
items.text: Thank you for letting me know, Admiral. At the moment they start the ritual, they'll be their most vulnerable. I need to be close to its center at that time.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Understood. You know what you're doing. I believe in you.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Their defenses are weak. There's no need to worry, Ms. Urd. Everything will go smoothly.

items.speaker: Urd
items.text: I'm not worried about myself. I'm worried about her.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: You mean your daughter?

items.speaker: Urd
items.text: Yes. She's still too young to understand all this.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The SPDM will take good care of her.

items.speaker: Urd
items.text: The Foundation made the same promise. I suppose it's the only way.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Manus Vindictae held its first space-time ritual on December 31st, 1999.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: If they had succeeded, that ritual would have brought time back to the Blank Era. Antarctica was their second attempt.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The results were much the same. The "Flood" summoned by the ritual was incomplete and turned into the first "Storm."
Footsteps echo through the long-sealed subway station, drawing them ever closer to the heart of the secret.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I promised Urd the operation would go smoothly, but I lied. Neither Zeno nor the Foundation had any idea how powerful the Manus's defensive ritual was.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The situation was desperate. We had only one order: advance, regardless of the casualties.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: When the "Storm" rose, it swallowed the details of the war. Yet the weight of it haunts me still—the grief of sending my soldiers to die.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Like the flame of a candle, they were extinguished in an instant.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: If it weren't for the "Storm" blurring my memories, I would've left Zeno and the Foundation far sooner.
The subway station ends, and ahead of them lies a broader space, where white light and air pour in.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Then, what ultimately led to your betrayal?
Igor halts and turns toward an obscure door at the corner of the hall.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: We've arrived.
It's carved from the same smooth marble as the surrounding wall, its outline only perceptible on close inspection. Unobtrusive, unremarkable even, but ever so mysterious.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: It was the Amber Room Project. It showed me the Pax House's arrogance.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: By now, I don't know which shows less respect for life, the Foundation or Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: I once thought that we fought and sacrificed for a firm conviction, to bring a bright and peaceful future.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: But I can fool myself no longer. The Pax House may aim to build a peaceful future for both humans and arcanists, but their means are no longer justifiable.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: And, with Arcana as She is, this is a war for gods. How can we stand—let alone claim victory—as mere mortals?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: How I wish to have a god on my side, Timekeeper.
There is an almost pleading note in his voice.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: What lies in the Amber Room, I cannot fully say. Data fragments, Ms. Urd's words, whatever it is, she wants you to have it.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Destiny has seen it survive several "Storms," waiting for this hour, for you.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: This is a door only you and Ms. Urd may open. Go. Walk through it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm still not sure if you're telling the truth, but thank you for bringing me here, Igor.
